output.title: Measuring late payment terms without guessing
output.body:
If you want to measure late payment terms, keep the decision narrow: are you still tracking due dates, agreed terms, actual payment dates, and follow-up status by memory or spreadsheet, or do you already have a repeatable check that flags overdue invoices before they turn into a cash-flow surprise?

That is the first workflow worth considering. Not a finance redesign, just one recurring task: compare the invoice date, agreed net terms, and payment date; flag anything past due; and keep a simple log of what was late. If a collection action follows, a human approves it. Money movement stays human.

The useful test is simple: how many invoices do you issue each month, and how do you currently know which ones are late? If that answer depends on manual review or memory, the workflow is probably frequent enough to inspect. If it is already reliable and low-effort, automation may not be worth adding.

A practical next step is to audit one week of invoices. Note which were paid on time, which were late, and how long the manual review took. That gives you a bounded picture of the work before you decide whether a pilot is worth it. Small-business finance is rarely glamorous; it is usually just repetitive.
